<!--

issue_context.title: ZHA setup failed after upgrade to 2023.3.x
issue_context.body:
### The problem

After upgrading to 2023.3.0 or .1 from 2023.2.5 ZHA fails to start with a stack trace ending in ~"unable to convert port to int". It seems as though it is possible before now to configure zha with an errant space at the end of the port #.

I have fixed by finding and removing the space in core.config_entries then restarting HA but it would be great to find and catch this during upgrade checks or the issues page.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.3.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2023.2.5

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

ZHA

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/zha/

### Diagnostics information

N/A - already resolved

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
N/A - UI setup
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
N/A - already resolved
```


### Additional information

_No response_

Reconfigure zha is integration and enter the url without the trailing space

> I have fixed by finding and removing the space in core.config_entries then restarting HA 

To confirm, the exact string in your config entry JSON was something like this?

```json
"socket://1.2.3.4:5678 "
```

> > I have fixed by finding and removing the space in core.config_entries then restarting HA
> 
> To confirm, the exact string in your config entry JSON was something like this?
> 
> ```json
> "socket://1.2.3.4:5678 "
> ```

Correct yes. Assuming during UI setup I copied it in with a trailing space by accident. It hasn't caused a running issue just after the upgrade this is shown.

I also ran into this.  Cleaning core.config_entries and restarting HA fixed it.

Would it be possible to add a check to the setup dialog to prevent this on new setups, and/or add a chomp to the config parsing?
